title: FL-Forensics: A Forensic-Ready Framework for Tamper-Evident Accountability and Auditability in Federated Learning
content: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing raw data, but existing defenses provide limited support for post-incident accountability and evidence preservation. We present FL-Forensics, a forensic-ready framework for malicious-client and compromised-aggregator settings. It combines client-signed update commitments, a hash-chained ledger, an independent evidence witness, trusted timestamping, key-lifecycle management, encrypted role-based storage, and permissioned quorum anchoring. We also introduce a Forensic Quality Index (FQI) with metrics for integrity, attribution, evidence availability, and audit efficiency. We implement FL-Forensics as an end-to-end Flower extension and evaluate it with 20 clients, Dirichlet non-IID data, and 15% malicious clients on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-100. It achieves F1 scores of 0.941, 0.800, and 0.521, with corresponding FQI values of 0.956, 0.900, and 0.714. Ablation results show that independent witnessing, digital signatures, trusted time, and external anchoring make distinct contributions to forensic recovery, attribution, and auditability under controlled evidence-tampering attacks.
